messages:
Julie: FYI customer X seeing a spike of 5xx + gateway timeouts on hosted inference since ~11:02. They say requests hang ~15s then 502/504. Escalation ticket opened.
Emma: thx, can you paste a sample request id / time window?
Julie: Request ids: req-9876, req-9879. Error graph: https://grafana/redwood/dashboard/abc -> 11:02-11:12 spike. P50 still ok, but p95/p99 skyrockets.
Raj: I see matching scale events — lots of concurrent cold starts. HPA shows pods ramping 0->6 repeatedly. Might be oscillation.
Mike: any KEDA ScaledObject attached to the queue? Customer uses our hosted queue trigger + KEDA, right?
Julie: yes, they use KEDA on burst-plan, configured by support.
ops-bot: Incident severity: P2 -> P1? ops-bot: auto-suggest runbook: autoscaling-scaleup-lag (https://runbooks/internal/autoscale) :eyes:
Emma: @Raj can you pull the HPA + KEDA events and the pod startup logs for that time range? Also readinessProbe times.
Raj: grabbing now. Quick paste:
```
kubectl get hpa -n infra-customer-x
NAME         REFERENCE                   TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
api-hpa      Deployment/api               80%/250m  0         20        0->6->1->5 pattern
```
Events: many "ScalingReplicaSet" events, then repeated FailedCreatePodSandBox for some nodes with msg "image pull backoff" (small frequency) but majority are normal. KEDA ScaledObject showed scaledownCooldown 30s and pollingInterval 15s.
Mike: that cooldown is short for GPU-backed cold starts. If scaledownCooldown is 30s we'll thrash on bursts. Also our model-init time is ~6-8s (KV cache miss). Combined that's causing request queue buildup.
Julie: customer reported 80 concurrent requests in a short window from their load test. They also use short client timeouts (10s), hence 504s.
Emma: repro plan: recreate a burst with 80 concurrent requests, track queue depth, and capture k8s events. I suspect KEDA's triggerThreshold and scaledownCooldown plus HPA minReplicas=0 lead to insufficient baseline capacity.
Raj: found relevant snippet in their ScaledObject:
```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
spec:
  cooldownPeriod: 30   # seconds
  pollingInterval: 15
  triggers:
  - type: rabbitmq
    metadata:
      queueLength: "50"
```
They set queueLength 50 which means only after >50 queued will it scale. With bursts of short spikes we hit queue backlog before scale completes.
Mike: also their deployment has `readinessProbe` with initialDelaySeconds: 20 and startupProbe absent. That delays traffic to new pods even after the process is running. Combined with model init makes end-to-end scale-up > 20s.
Julie: customer timeouts at 10s, so if scale-up path takes >10s we see 504s.
Emma: actions: 1) advise customer to raise client timeout temporarily while we mitigate. 2) increase minReplicas to 2 during predicted bursts. 3) adjust KEDA queueLength -> 10 and cooldown->120s OR use externalScaledObject with prewarm. 4) add startupProbe + reduce readiness initialDelay.
Raj: I'm running a small test in staging with same config but changed queueLength to 10 and minReplicas=2. Running a synthetic burst now.
ops-bot: Deploy job queued: deploy/staging-autoscale-test started by Raj at 11:26.
Raj: test results: with minReplicas=0 we saw requests queue and p99 latency > 20s -> 504s. With minReplicas=2 and queueLength=10, p99 dropped to ~6.5s and no 504s for 80 concurrent burst.
Mike: logs from a cold pod: model init 6.2s, readiness probe delay 18s (initialDelay 20), container started but not marked ready for 20s. So the readiness probe is the dominant extra delay.
Emma: propose we ship a config checklist to support: for GPU inference services: - minReplicas >= 1 for bursty customers - KEDA queueLength <= expected burst - cooldown >= modelInitSeconds*2 - add startupProbe configured to detect model-ready earlier - set readiness initialDelay to <5s or remove if startupProbe covers it
Julie: I'll send recommendations to customer with test evidence and temporary workaround: bump client timeout to 30s and schedule a config change window.
Mike: longer-term: add a platform-level prewarm pool for hosted tier (small always-on pool) and a circuit-breaker at gateway so downstream sees 429 instead of long 504s during scale.
Emma: agreed. For this incident, status: mitigation validated in staging. Raj -> please open a PR template that updates our support templates and autoscale runbook with those knobs.
Raj: on it. I'll also attach the k8s events dump and the test artifact in the ticket.
Julie: customer accepted workaround and will schedule the change. Closing loop: leaving incident thread open for 24h to verify no recurrence. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident updated: P1 -> monitoring for 24h.
Mike: note for eng-runtime: consider exposing model init histogram in metrics to better tune cooldown.
Emma: adding to backlog.
Julie: thanks team. I'll post the support ticket link and the config diffs in the ticket.
Emma: great, marking this resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
